literal: Wei Shenyuan Empress Dowager Dou; Wendi Empress Feng; Huandi Empress Wei; Pingwen Empress Wang; Zhaocheng Empress Murong; Xianming Empress He; Daowu Empress Murong; Daowu Xuanmu Empress Liu; Mingyuan Zhaoguai Empress Yao; Mingyuan secret Empress Du; Taiwu Empress Helian; Taiwu Jing'ai Empress He; Jingmu Gong Empress Yujiulü; Wencheng Civilizing Empress Feng; Wencheng Yuan Empress Li; Xianwen Si Empress Li; Xiaowen Zhen Empress Lin; Xiaowen deposed Empress Feng; Xiaowen You Empress Feng; Xiaowen Wenzhao Empress Gao; Xuanwu Shun Empress Yu; Xuanwu Empress Gao; Xuanwu Ling Empress Hu; Xiaoming Empress Hu; Xiaowu Empress Gao; Wendi Wen Empress Yifu; Wendi Dao Empress Yujiulü; Deposed Emperor Empress Yuwen; Gongdi Empress Ruogan; Xiaojing Empress Gao

literal: Han followed Qin institutions: the emperor's grandmother was called Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, his consort Empress; the rest were mostly called Lady, increased or reduced with the age—not like the Zhou Rites' fixed numbers of ladies, consorts, wives, and attendants.
idiomatic: The Han followed Qin institutions: the emperor's grandmother was called grand empress dowager, his mother empress dowager, his consort empress; the rest were mostly called lady, increased or reduced with the times—not like the fixed numbers of ladies, consorts, wives, and attendants in the Zhou Rites.

literal: Wei and Jin followed one another, with promotions and demotions from time to time; earlier histories have stated this fully.
idiomatic: Wei and Jin followed one another, with titles rising and falling from time to time; earlier histories have stated this fully.

literal: Though the Wei royal enterprise began with Shenyuan, before Zhaocheng the regulations of the six palaces were not fully set forth;
idiomatic: Though the Wei royal enterprise began with Shenyuan, before Zhaocheng the regulations of the six palaces were not fully set forth;

literal: and of the eight emperors Zhang, Ping, Si, Zhao, Mu, Hui, Yang, and Lie, the consorts are not recorded.
idiomatic: and of the eight emperors Zhang, Ping, Si, Zhao, Mu, Hui, Yang, and Lie, the consorts are not recorded.

literal: Daowu posthumously honored his ancestresses, all taking the emperor's posthumous title as empress.
idiomatic: Daowu posthumously honored his ancestresses, all taking the emperor's posthumous title as empress.

literal: He first established the central palace; other concubines might be called lady, without limit in number, yet all had grades.
idiomatic: He first established the central palace; other concubines might be called lady, without limit in number, yet all had grades.

literal: Taiwu gradually added left and right zhaoyi and noble ladies, pepper chambers, and the like; the rear apartments grew numerous.
idiomatic: Taiwu gradually added left and right zhaoyi, noble ladies, pepper chambers, and the like; the rear apartments grew numerous.

literal: Again, by Wei precedent, when about to establish an empress, she had to cast a golden figure by hand—success was auspicious, otherwise she could not be established.
idiomatic: Again, by Wei precedent, when about to establish an empress, she had to cast a golden figure by hand—success was auspicious, otherwise she could not be established.

literal: Again, for Taiwu and Wencheng, the toil of wet-nurses was honored to the utmost—though it deviated from ritual, one may know benevolence by observing excess.
idiomatic: Again, for Taiwu and Wencheng, the toil of wet-nurses was honored to the utmost—though it deviated from ritual, one may know benevolence by observing excess.

literal: Xiaowen reformed inner offices: left and right zhaoyi ranked with the grand marshal; three ladies with the three dukes; three pin with the three ministers; six pin with the six ministers; world wives with chief grand masters; palace women with yuan shi.
idiomatic: Xiaowen reformed inner offices: left and right zhaoyi ranked with the grand marshal; three ladies with the three dukes; three pin with the three ministers; six pin with the six ministers; world wives with chief grand masters; palace women with yuan shi.

literal: Later female offices were added to administer the inner bureau.
idiomatic: Later female offices were added to administer the inner bureau.

literal: The inner bureau ranked with the director and vice director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: The inner bureau ranked with the director and vice director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Director of works, grand supervisor, and female attendant-in-chief—three offices ranked as second grade.
idiomatic: Director of works, grand supervisor, and female attendant-in-chief—three offices ranked as second grade.

literal: Supervisor, female master of writing, beauties, female scribes, female worthies, female recorders, writing women, and junior writing women—five offices ranked as third grade.
idiomatic: Supervisor, female master of writing, beauties, female scribes, female worthies, female recorders, writing women, and junior writing women—five offices ranked as third grade.

literal: Middle talents, attendants, middle envoys, palace female talents, and respectful palace women ranked as fourth grade.
idiomatic: Middle talents, attendants, middle envoys, palace female talents, and respectful palace women ranked as fourth grade.

literal: Green robes, female wine, female feast, female food, and Xian official female slaves ranked as fifth grade.
idiomatic: Green robes, female wine, female feast, female food, and Xian official female slaves ranked as fifth grade.

literal: As for Qi Shenwu and Wenxiang, both had not yet reached the supreme throne.
idiomatic: As for Qi Shenwu and Wenxiang, both had not yet reached the supreme throne.

literal: Shenwu's principal wife was called consort; the Rouran woman he married was called Princess Rouran.
idiomatic: Shenwu's principal wife was called consort; the Rouran woman he married was called Princess Rouran.

literal: Wenxiang had married a Wei princess, hence no separate title.
idiomatic: Wenxiang had married a Wei princess, hence no separate title.

literal: In both palaces, other concubines were all called niang only.
idiomatic: In both palaces, other concubines were all called niang only.

literal: Wenxuan's rear apartments had titles of lady, pin, and imperial attendant, but the quotas were not fixed.
idiomatic: Wenxuan's rear apartments had titles of lady, pin, and imperial attendant, but the quotas were not fixed.

literal: Xiaozhao's inner offices were very few; only Consort Yang, with talent and beauty together, was also of a noble house; Sang, mother of the Prince of Xiangcheng, had virtue and conduct—both received favor and courtesy; the rest are not recorded.
idiomatic: Xiaozhao's inner offices were very few; only Consort Yang, with talent and beauty together, was also of a noble house; Sang, mother of the Prince of Xiangcheng, had virtue and conduct—both received favor and courtesy; the rest are not recorded.

literal: Heqing new statutes: inner titled ladies followed antiquity with three ladies, nine pin, twenty-seven world wives, and eighty-one palace women.
idiomatic: Heqing new statutes: inner titled ladies followed antiquity with three ladies, nine pin, twenty-seven world wives, and eighty-one palace women.

literal: Again following Han institutions, zhaoyi were established, left and right, two persons, ranking with the chancellor.
idiomatic: Again following Han institutions, zhaoyi were established, left and right, two persons, ranking with the chancellor.

literal: Hongde, Zhengde, and Chongde were the three ladies, ranking with the three dukes.
idiomatic: Hongde, Zhengde, and Chongde were the three ladies, ranking with the three dukes.

literal: Guangyou, Zhaoxun, and Longhui were upper pin, ranking with the three ministers.
idiomatic: Guangyou, Zhaoxun, and Longhui were upper pin, ranking with the three ministers.

literal: Xuanhui, Ninghui, Xuanming, Shunhua, Ninghua, and Guangxun were lower pin, ranking with the six ministers.
idiomatic: Xuanhui, Ninghui, Xuanming, Shunhua, Ninghua, and Guangxun were lower pin, ranking with the six ministers.

literal: Wucheng loved the inner quarters and filled all quotas; besides these he also set talents and caicai as loose titles.
idiomatic: Wucheng loved the inner quarters and filled all quotas; besides these he also set talents and caicai as loose titles.

literal: Later, when the king established two empresses, below zhaoyi all numbers were doubled.
idiomatic: Later, when the king established two empresses, below zhaoyi all numbers were doubled.

literal: Left and right Eying were also added, ranking with left and right chancellors; zhaoyi was lowered to rank with second grand masters.
idiomatic: Left and right Eying were also added, ranking with left and right chancellors; zhaoyi was lowered to rank with second grand masters.

literal: Soon a shufei was added, one person, ranking with the prime minister.
idiomatic: Soon a shufei was added, one person, ranking with the prime minister.

literal: The Zhou followed the Ji institutions; inner offices were orderly.
idiomatic: The Zhou followed the Ji institutions; inner offices were orderly.

literal: Wendi in founding the state kept bed and mat frugal;
idiomatic: Wendi in founding the state kept bed and mat frugal;

literal: Wuhuang succeeding the throne restrained passion in correcting excess.
idiomatic: Wuhuang succeeding the throne restrained passion in correcting excess.

literal: The palace had the beauty of strung fish; the imperial kin had no fault of private favoritism—this may be called grasping the ruler's substance.
idiomatic: The palace had the beauty of strung fish; the imperial kin had no fault of private favoritism—this may be called grasping the ruler's substance.

literal: Xuanhuang outwardly pursued his aims, inwardly indulged his desires; ravines and gullies could not be filled, selection without end;
idiomatic: Xuanhuang outwardly pursued his aims, inwardly indulged his desires; ravines and gullies could not be filled, selection without end;

literal: where favor reached, none was limited to menials;
idiomatic: where favor reached, none was limited to menials;

literal: where glory extended, none was barred by danger or flattery.
idiomatic: where glory extended, none was barred by danger or flattery.

literal: Thus those who ascended the orchid hall for the principal place and trod the pepper courtyard as equals were not one;
idiomatic: Thus those who ascended the orchid hall for the principal place and trod the pepper courtyard as equals were not one;

literal: those who by the curtain dragged blue and purple and by favor clutched jade and silk were not one clan.
idiomatic: those who by the curtain dragged blue and purple and by favor clutched jade and silk were not one clan.

literal: Though the debauchery of Xin and Gui and the ruin wrought by Zhao and Li scarcely suffice to compare in likeness.
idiomatic: Though the debauchery of Xin and Gui and the ruin wrought by Zhao and Li scarcely suffice to compare in likeness.

literal: Men weary of harsh government; abuses were many—Wendi's sacrifices suddenly ended, especially for this reason.
idiomatic: Men weary of harsh government; abuses were many—Wendi's sacrifices suddenly ended, especially for this reason.

literal: Sui Wendi wished to reform former abuses and greatly correct their violations; only the empress held the house, with no private favorites at her side;
idiomatic: Sui Wendi wished to reform former abuses and greatly correct their violations; only the empress held the house, with no private favorites at her side;

literal: women's offices and titles were not yet fully detailed.
idiomatic: women's offices and titles were not yet fully detailed.

literal: In the second year of Kaihuang the form of inner offices was set, roughly following the Zhou Rites, reducing their number.
idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang the form of inner offices was set, roughly following the Zhou Rites, reducing their number.

literal: Three pin, teaching the four virtues, ranked regular third grade;
idiomatic: Three pin, teaching the four virtues, ranked regular third grade;

literal: nine world wives, managing guests and sacrifices, ranked regular fifth grade;
idiomatic: nine world wives, managing guests and sacrifices, ranked regular fifth grade;

literal: thirty-eight palace women, managing women's work and silk, ranked regular seventh grade.
idiomatic: thirty-eight palace women, managing women's work and silk, ranked regular seventh grade.

literal: Again adopting Han and Jin old rites, six Shang, six Si, and six Dian were set, each supervising the next, to govern palace affairs.
idiomatic: Again adopting Han and Jin old rites, six Shang, six Si, and six Dian were set, each supervising the next, to govern palace affairs.

literal: First, Shang Palace, guiding the empress and inner gates' grants.
idiomatic: First, Shang Palace, guiding the empress and inner gates' grants.

literal: It oversaw three Ling Si, managing registers and laws, investigating and memorializing;
idiomatic: It oversaw three Ling Si, managing registers and laws, investigating and memorializing;

literal: three Dian Cong, managing seals and ritual vessels.
idiomatic: three Dian Cong, managing seals and ritual vessels.

literal: Second, Shang Ceremonial, managing ritual and instruction.
idiomatic: Second, Shang Ceremonial, managing ritual and instruction.

literal: It oversaw three Si Yue, managing music;
idiomatic: It oversaw three Si Yue, managing music;

literal: three Dian Zan, guiding inner and outer titled ladies in audience.
idiomatic: three Dian Zan, guiding inner and outer titled ladies in audience.

literal: Third, Shang Robes, managing garments and treasures.
idiomatic: Third, Shang Robes, managing garments and treasures.

literal: It oversaw three Si Shi, managing hairpins, earrings, flowers, and adornment;
idiomatic: It oversaw three Si Shi, managing hairpins, earrings, flowers, and adornment;

literal: three Dian Ji, managing towels, combs, and bathing.
idiomatic: three Dian Ji, managing towels, combs, and bathing.

literal: Fourth, Shang Food, managing presentation and tasting first.
idiomatic: Fourth, Shang Food, managing presentation and tasting first.

literal: It oversaw three Si Yi, managing prescriptions, medicine, and divination;
idiomatic: It oversaw three Si Yi, managing prescriptions, medicine, and divination;

literal: three Dian Qi, managing goblets and vessels.
idiomatic: three Dian Qi, managing goblets and vessels.

literal: Fifth, Shang Quarters, managing curtains, bedding, and mats.
idiomatic: Fifth, Shang Quarters, managing curtains, bedding, and mats.

literal: It oversaw three Si Yan, managing spreading, sprinkling, and sweeping;
idiomatic: It oversaw three Si Yan, managing spreading, sprinkling, and sweeping;

literal: three Dian Zhi, managing fans, umbrellas, lamps, and candles.
idiomatic: three Dian Zhi, managing fans, umbrellas, lamps, and candles.

literal: Sixth, Shang Works, managing construction and the hundred tasks.
idiomatic: Sixth, Shang Works, managing construction and the hundred tasks.

literal: It oversaw three Si Zhi, managing clothes and cutting;
idiomatic: It oversaw three Si Zhi, managing clothes and cutting;

literal: three Dian Hui, managing wealth in and out.
idiomatic: three Dian Hui, managing wealth in and out.

literal: Each of the six Shang had three posts ranked sub-ninth grade; six Si ranked merit grades; six Dian ranked outer-flow second grade.
idiomatic: Each of the six Shang had three posts ranked sub-ninth grade; six Si ranked merit grades; six Dian ranked outer-flow second grade.

literal: At first, Empress Dowager Wenxian's merit joined in founding trials; outwardly she took part in court government, inwardly she monopolized the palace;
idiomatic: At first, Empress Dowager Wenxian's merit joined in founding trials; outwardly she took part in court government, inwardly she monopolized the palace;

literal: bearing a jealous heart, she left pin and concubine posts empty;
idiomatic: bearing a jealous heart, she left pin and concubine posts empty;

literal: she did not set the three consorts, guarding against their pressing from above.
idiomatic: she did not set the three consorts, guarding against their pressing from above.

literal: From pin downward, sixty posts were set.
idiomatic: From pin downward, sixty posts were set.

literal: She further reduced and restrained insignia, lowering their ranks.
idiomatic: She further reduced and restrained insignia, lowering their ranks.

literal: After Wenxian's death, three noble ladies were first set; pin increased to nine, world wives twenty-seven, palace women eighty-one.
idiomatic: After Wenxian's death, three noble ladies were first set; pin increased to nine, world wives twenty-seven, palace women eighty-one.

literal: Noble ladies and the like oversaw palace affairs; below the six Shang all were divided among them.
idiomatic: Noble ladies and the like oversaw palace affairs; below the six Shang all were divided among them.

literal: Under Yangdi, empresses, pin, and attendants had no clear women's duties—only proper bearing and fine adornment, accompanying banquets and tours.
idiomatic: Under Yangdi, empresses, pin, and attendants had no clear women's duties—only proper bearing and fine adornment, accompanying banquets and tours.

literal: The emperor also examined precedents, devised fine names himself, and set them in edicts.
idiomatic: The emperor also examined precedents, devised fine names himself, and set them in edicts.

literal: Guifei, shufei, and defei were the three ladies, rank first positive.
idiomatic: Guifei, shufei, and defei were the three ladies, rank first positive.

literal: Shunyi, shunrong, shunhua, xiuyi, xiurong, xiuhua, chongyi, chongrong, and chonghua were the nine pin, rank second positive.
idiomatic: Shunyi, shunrong, shunhua, xiuyi, xiurong, xiuhua, chongyi, chongrong, and chonghua were the nine pin, rank second positive.

literal: Jieyu, twelve posts, rank third positive.
idiomatic: Jieyu, twelve posts, rank third positive.

literal: Meiren and cairen, fifteen posts, rank fourth positive—these were world wives.
idiomatic: Meiren and cairen, fifteen posts, rank fourth positive—these were world wives.

literal: Baolin, twenty posts, rank fifth positive.
idiomatic: Baolin, twenty posts, rank fifth positive.

literal: Palace women, twenty-four posts, rank sixth positive.
idiomatic: Palace women, twenty-four posts, rank sixth positive.

literal: Cainü, thirty-seven posts, rank seventh positive—these were nüyu; in all one hundred twenty, ordered for the feast-bed chamber.
idiomatic: Cainü, thirty-seven posts, rank seventh positive—these were nüyu; in all one hundred twenty, ordered for the feast-bed chamber.

literal: There were also chengyi and daoren, all attending left and right, without fixed number, regarded as sixth grade and below.
idiomatic: There were also chengyi and daoren, all attending left and right, without fixed number, regarded as sixth grade and below.

literal: At the time female offices were further added, modeled on the Masters of Writing, with six bureaus governing twenty-four offices.
idiomatic: At the time female offices were further added, modeled on the Masters of Writing, with six bureaus governing twenty-four offices.

literal: First, Shang Palace Bureau, overseeing Si Yan, managing proclamation and memorials;
idiomatic: First, Shang Palace Bureau, overseeing Si Yan, managing proclamation and memorials;

literal: Si Bu, managing registers and accounts;
idiomatic: Si Bu, managing registers and accounts;

literal: Si Zheng, managing forms and punishments;
idiomatic: Si Zheng, managing forms and punishments;

idiomatic: Si Wei, managing gates and keys.

idiomatic: Second, Shang Ceremonial Bureau, overseeing Si Ji, managing classics, history, teaching, paper, brush, and tables;

literal: Si Yue, managing pitch and law;
idiomatic: Si Yue, managing pitch and law;

literal: Si Bin, managing guests;
idiomatic: Si Bin, managing guests;

literal: Si Zan, managing ritual and assisting guidance.
idiomatic: Si Zan, managing ritual and assisting guidance.

literal: Third, Shang Robes Bureau, overseeing Si Xi, managing seals and tallies;
idiomatic: Third, Shang Robes Bureau, overseeing Si Xi, managing seals and tallies;

literal: Si Yi, managing clothes;
idiomatic: Si Yi, managing clothes;
